Extended remediation notes

  1. Immediately prioritize internet-reachable mod_php and other web-facing PHP (FPM, CGI, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed). Determine network reachability separately; this is NOT an external exposure scan.
  2. Apply upstream PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 or your vendor's verified equivalent patches. Restart/recycle all PHP workers, pools and services; re-scan and verify the active web-serving SAPI and container images.
  3. If patching must be delayed: consider administratively enforced memory_limit=-1, conservative post_max_size and edge request bounds for CVE-2026-109618; these are incomplete risk reductions and have availability tradeoffs.
  4. For CVE-2026-109619, administratively disable session.upload_progress.enabled and restart all workers; on PHP 8.5, consider fatal_error_backtraces=0 until patched. Neither measure covers every attack path.
  5. Confirm WAF/origin access cannot be bypassed and document time-bounded restrictions if a patch cannot be deployed immediately.
  6. Preserve and review access/error logs and EDR telemetry from before patching; patched servers may already have been compromised. A clean IOC result does not rule out compromise.
  7. See official advisories: https://www.php.net/ and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp

Exploitation attempts: NOT_ASSESSED  ·  Possible compromise: NOT_ASSESSED  ·  Investigation coverage: NOT_REQUESTED

Statuses are independent. This tool never claims a host is clean or confirmed compromised. Long request-target length, large HTTP bodies, unusual form-field names, and multipart nesting are distinct signals; ordinary access logs typically provide only the first (URI length heuristic). Blocked WAF actions are not successful exploitation. WAF leads do not alone set possible-compromise. Do not claim two requests shared a PHP worker without worker identity evidence.

Configured SAPI hints: Observed configured/inventory hints: PHP-FPM (binary/package/process or FastCGI proxy hints). These artifacts do NOT prove which SAPI currently serves HTTP. Calif research: mod_php may continue into request shutdown / worker reuse after some startup fatals; PHP-FPM terminates the worker on php_request_startup failure (FPM_EXIT_SOFTWARE) but can still be exploited after successful startup (application-dependent decode + upload-progress paths). Do not infer that PHP-FPM cannot be exploited. Patch and verify the active serving runtime separately.
HTTP body / form metadata: Not available from ordinary access logs. Prefer offline WAF exports with documented fields. Content-Length and multipart nesting are not inferred from URI lines.
Observed PHP configuration: Whitelisted php.ini settings are static text only (OBSERVED≠EFFECTIVE). Temporary mitigations such as session.upload_progress.enabled or memory_limit changes are unverified and do not replace patching.
